topics.title: How do we assess democracy's outcomes?

concepts.learning_objective: Recall the reasons democracy is considered better than other forms of government and the gap between its principle and practice.
Explain that democracy is only a form of government that creates conditions which citizens must use to achieve goals.
Explain how democracy produces a government that follows procedures, is transparent and is accountable to citizens.
Evaluate the argument that the delay caused by deliberation makes democratic government inefficient.
Explain why democratic government is legitimate and enjoys overwhelming popular support.
Interpret evidence comparing economic growth rates of democracies and dictatorships between 1950 and 2000.
Identify the factors other than the form of government on which economic development depends.
Distinguish political equality in voting from the growing economic inequalities found in democracies.
Interpret data on the share of national income held by the top and bottom 20 per cent in selected democracies.
Analyse why democratically elected governments have not been very successful in reducing poverty.
Explain how democracies develop procedures to negotiate social differences and prevent them from turning violent.
State the two conditions a democracy must fulfil to accommodate social diversity.

topics.title: Dignity and freedom of the citizens

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how recognition of equality in democracy strengthens the struggles of women and disadvantaged castes.
Interpret why public complaints about democracy are a sign of its success in turning subjects into citizens.
